requirements.text: The NLM Digital Repository must be designed with regard to international best practice for digital archives/repositories.
The NLM Digital Repository must support the acceptance and preservation of material that is provided in non-preferred formats or non-standard formats.
The repository system must include the ability to record all actions and decisions made concerning the submitted material.
The system must maintain the relationship between the parent object and any subsequent child objects.
The NLM Repository system must be compatible with and conform to the requirements of the NIH Consolidated Collocation Site (NCCS), NLM's off-site back-up facility.
The Library will not provide offline delivery services.
The amount of redundant data stored in the object should be kept to a minimum required for identification of the object.
The NLM Digital Repository must implement role-based access control (RBAC) and encryption at rest and in transit, compliant with NIST SP 800-53 moderate baseline controls.
The system must provide a response time of under 2 seconds for 95% of search queries while implementing rate-limiting to prevent resource exhaustion.
The system must perform automated virus and malware scanning on all incoming SIPs prior to staging, with a defined quarantine and notification workflow for detected threats.
The system must provide a search response time of less than 2 seconds for 95% of queries under normal load.
The repository architecture must support an initial ingest of [X] TB and a projected annual growth of [Y] TB, with horizontal scaling capabilities for storage.
The system must achieve an RPO of less than 1 hour and an RTO of less than 24 hours for critical repository services.
The system must perform automated bit-level integrity checks (fixity) on all stored objects at least annually, with a 99.999% success rate in detecting and reporting corruption.
The system must provide search results for 95% of queries in under 2 seconds under a load of 50 concurrent users.
The system must support an initial ingest capacity of [X] TB and a sustained throughput of [Y] GB/hour for bulk ingest operations.
The storage hierarchy must support a minimum read throughput of [X] MB/s for concurrent access to high-demand digital objects.
